Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Goal: Support Optix Health's clinical summarization and charting assistant under predictable latency (p95 < 250ms) with embeddings-based similarity search for patient notes and a lightweight reranker for top-k results.
- Traffic profile you shared: ~2.5M tokens/day currently, expected to grow to ~10M tokens/day in 6 months; peak concurrent inference requests ~45 QPS, average request size ~120 tokens.
- Key integration points: SDK setup (server-side for backend), OAuth2 / SSO for per-user scoping, routing for region failover, tool-calling support for structured output (JSON schema), embeddings + reranker pipeline.

Ask from Optix to validate for sizing:
1) Confirm 95th percentile request size and expected peak QPS per region.
2) Any additional batching constraints (max latency per user operation).
3) Will you host the model in Dedicated (reserved pool) or require Private (VPC)? We discussed Dedicated as the likely path.

What we propose next:
- Marissa (SE) to run a quick traffic-to-capacity sizing sketch and propose an autoscaling policy (min/max nodes, warm pool, burst behavior).
- Technical deep-dive (30-45m) to walk through SDK auth patterns, prefix caching, KV cache handling for chat, and embedding/re-ranker throughput trade-offs. Suggested times: Wed/Thu this week.

I've attached a short traffic export (optix-traffic-summary.csv) and a rough sketch you sent during the call (optix-arch-sketch.png) — thanks for sharing.

If that looks right, reply with preferred time for the deep-dive and the missing QPS/token percentiles.

Thanks,

Hi Emily / Aditya —

Thanks for the numbers — this is helpful. A few notes from the SE sizing perspective and items for the deep-dive:

Sizing sketch (initial):
- Workload: mix of short chat requests (median 95 tokens) and summary jobs (tail up to 220 tokens).
- For p95 < 250ms and ~35 peak QPS in us-east, we'd recommend an initial Dedicated pool sized for sustained 40 QPS (to allow headroom + small burst). That typically maps to N GPU nodes depending on model choice (e.g., ggml-quantized v2 on A100 vs 8-bit LLM). We'll provide a model-specific mapping in the deep-dive.
- Autoscaling policy: min nodes = capacity to handle baseline 10 QPS (warm pool), max nodes = capacity for 120 QPS (burst). Use fast scale-up (target 30s) with pre-warmed instances for predicted bursts and slightly slower scale-down (5-10min) to avoid thrash.
- Concurrency: set per-node concurrency = 4 for long-sequence workloads; use request-level queueing with max queue delay 150ms to preserve interactivity.

Integration notes:
- SDK: we recommend server-side SDK + short-lived tokens for requests (service tokens for backend operations). We'll send code samples for OAuth2 + service account flow.
- Auth: support for SAML SSO + SCIM is available for Private; for Dedicated we support SSO and API keys with RBAC.
- Embeddings/reranker: run embeddings offline into a vector DB; real-time reranking can be done on top of top-100 candidates. We'll discuss batching and async callbacks in the deep-dive.

Action items for deep-dive:
1) Go over model mapping table (we'll bring model throughput numbers).
2) Validate queuing behavior and acceptable queue delay for your UI flows.
3) Walk through SDK auth samples and a canary rollout plan (traffic slice, monitoring, fallback).

Emily — Wed 14:00 ET works for the team. Aditya / Dylan — I'll set an agenda and share a short doc beforehand.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
